studyPages.body:
EVERYDAY MEANING OF PRESSURE
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what everyday meaning of pressure means in plain words.
• Use one real Kenyan example to show everyday meaning of pressure.
• Correct one common mistake about everyday meaning of pressure.

INTRODUCTION
----
Carry a heavy bag on thin straps and your shoulders hurt; use wide padded straps and the same weight feels easier. The force did not change much — the area did. That everyday feeling is the doorway into pressure.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Pressure is defined as the force acting normally per unit area. Normally here means at a right angle or perpendicularly.
• In the scenario above, the girl makes deeper impressions on the muddy ground than the boy. This is because the weight of the boy is spread over a large surface area than that of the girl. The greater the force (weight) acts on, the less the effect or impression made on the muddy surface.
• The sharp heel shoes of the girl have a small surface area in contact with the ground. The smaller the area the deeper the impressions or more sinking than the shoes of the boy for the same weight.
• In this case, the bag with narrow straps will produce more squeezing effect than that one with wider straps for the same force (weight) of books carried. This is because, pressure is high when the surface area is small, and it is low when the surface area is large.
• Therefore, pressure is the force acting normally per unit area.
• Pressure is represented by a symbol “P”.
• It is defined as force acting normally per unit area applied to the surface of an object.

WORKED EXAMPLE
----
Worked situation (a hardware shop in Nakuru): a learner investigates everyday meaning of pressure. First observation: Pressure is defined as the force acting normally per unit area. Normally here means at a right angle or perpendicularly. Because of that observation, the learner names the correct scientific idea and rejects a near-miss confusion. So the conclusion is written in one accurate sentence that matches the main notes — with the correct symbol or formula if one applies (H₂O, NaCl, Fe, P = F / A).

studyPages.title: Formula P Equals F Over A
studyPages.body:
FORMULA P EQUALS F OVER A
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what formula p equals f over a means in plain words.
• Use one real Kenyan example to show formula p equals f over a.
• Correct one common mistake about formula p equals f over a.

INTRODUCTION
----
Stand on soft mud in sharp heels and you sink; stand in flat shoes and you may not. The force of your weight is similar, but the area changed. Pressure is force divided by area — P = F / A — which is why sharp tools cut and wide tyres float better on soft ground.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Pressure is the force acting normally (perpendicularly) on a unit area.
• The formula is P = F / A, where P is pressure, F is force in newtons (N), and A is area in square metres (m²).
• The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa). One pascal equals one newton per square metre (N/m²).
• If force stays the same and area gets smaller, pressure increases. If area gets larger, pressure decreases.

WORKED EXAMPLE
----
A delivery helper near Marikiti market in Nairobi pushes a cart.

First find the pressure when force is 200 N and area is 0.50 m².

Working:
1. Formula / relationship: P = F / A
2. Substitute values: P = 200 N / 0.5 m²
3. P = 400
Final Answer: 400 Pa (N/m²)
Mark reminder: method mark for substituting into P = F / A; accuracy mark for correct Pa value

Now compare: if the same 200 N acts on a narrower plank of 0.20 m², then P = 200 / 0.20 = 1000 Pa. Because pressure rose, the cart sinks more on soft ground. First we used P = F / A, then we substituted, then we compared areas — that is the reasoning.

IN EVERYDAY LIFE
----
At Marikiti market in Nairobi, formula p equals f over a shows up when you handle real materials or processes linked to this idea. Practical tip: write the correct symbol or formula before you explain out loud.

SUMMARY
----
• Pressure is the force acting normally (perpendicularly) on a unit area.
• The formula is P = F / A, where P is pressure, F is force in newtons (N), and A is area in square metres (m²).
• The SI unit of pressure is the pascal (Pa). One pascal equals one newton per square metre (N/m²).
• If force stays the same and area gets smaller, pressure increases. If area gets larger, pressure decreases.
